render.prompt:
Image 1 is a real phone photo of a room to edit. Image 2 is a placement guide: the same photo with numbered translucent boxes showing where each product goes; use it only for position and scale and never draw its boxes or numbers. Images 3 to 5 are the reference photos of products 1 to 3, in order.
1. Replace the dark brown 3-seat sofa with product 1: Modern Grey Linen Sofa (sofa), real size 198.1 x 96.5 x 88.9 cm (width x depth x height). Centered against window wall where old sofa stands, facing the TV, long side parallel to windows. It belongs inside box 1 of the placement guide. Copy product 1 exactly from its reference photo: Low rectangular three-seat sofa in light beige linen with loose back cushions, square arms, and tapered dark wood legs. Same shape, proportions, color, material, texture, pattern and details, scaled to its real size relative to the room.
2. Add product 2: Cream geometric wool area rug (rug), real size 243.8 x 152.4 x 1.3 cm (width x depth x height). Flat on wood floor under coffee table, long side parallel to sofa, centered between sofa and TV stand. It belongs inside box 2 of the placement guide. Copy product 2 exactly from its reference photo: Rectangular cream wool rug with subtle geometric criss-cross texture shown in angled perspective view. Same shape, proportions, color, material, texture, pattern and details, scaled to its real size relative to the room.
3. Add product 3: White Linen Swing Arm Floor Lamp (floor lamp), real size 38.1 x 38.1 x 160 cm (width x depth x height). Standing on floor in back corner between sofa right arm and TV stand, shade above eye level. It belongs inside box 3 of the placement guide. Copy product 3 exactly from its reference photo: Tall swing-arm floor lamp with large white linen drum shade on slender brushed nickel pole with adjustable joint. Same shape, proportions, color, material, texture, pattern and details, scaled to its real size relative to the room.
Hard rules: keep the exact same camera position, framing, lens distortion and perspective. Keep the walls, wallpaper, floor, ceiling, ceiling light, windows, blinds or curtains, doors and every object that is not listed exactly as they are. Keep the existing light direction, color temperature and exposure; new products receive the same light and cast soft, physically plausible contact shadows. The result must look like an unedited phone photo of the same room, not a render. Do not add anything else: no extra decor, no text, no numbers, no colored boxes or outlines.
